info.name: Buildiq Page Editor Integration
info.description:
Newman/Postman coverage for openspec change `buildiq-page-editor` (task 7 — integration). Reads, mutates and restores the hello-world manifest through buildiq's own manifest endpoint, verifying that a saved page is reflected on the next read and that a manifest the runtime cannot render is refused.

⚠️ THIS COLLECTION USED TO WRITE THE MANIFEST ONTO THE OR `Application` OBJECT, AND THAT IS WHY IT WAS RED.

Under the pre-ADR-002 model the manifest lived on the Application. It does not any more — lib/Settings/openbuild_register.json declares the `Application` schema with slug/name/description/appType/status/baseRef/productionVersion/icon/iconDark/allowUserOverrides/permissions/githubRepo/githubDefaultBranch and NO `manifest` property; the manifest is a property of `ApplicationVersion`. ApplicationsController:221-236 says so in as many words and reads through ManifestResolverService.

So `PUT /apps/openregister/api/objects/buildiq/application/{uuid}` with a `manifest` key wrote a property the schema does not carry. OR accepted it (200, and it even echoed the value back, which is why request 2's own assertion passed), but `GET /api/applications/hello-world/manifest` reads the production ApplicationVersion and never saw it. The same absence is why an invalid manifest came back 200: there was no `manifest` property for OR to validate, so there was nothing to reject.

Both requests now go to `PUT /index.php/apps/buildiq/api/applications/{slug}/manifest` (appinfo/routes.php, applications#saveManifest), which writes onto the production ApplicationVersion — the same record the GET reads. Note the asymmetry the route intends: GET returns the manifest bare, PUT expects it wrapped in `{ manifest }`.

Idempotent: request 5 restores the manifest captured in request 1.

item.name: 1. GET the hello-world manifest — capture it for the mutation and the restore

request.description: The read side of the pair under test. GET returns the manifest BARE (not wrapped), resolved from the production ApplicationVersion by ManifestResolverService.

exec: pm.test('the seeded manifest is a renderable shape — version + pages', function () {

item.name: 2. PUT the manifest with an added page — 200

request.description: Append a marker page to the captured manifest and save it. The response names its write target so a silent fallback to the legacy application-level manifest cannot pass unnoticed.

The write must be visible to the read the runtime actually performs. This is the assertion that was red: the old collection wrote to a property the Application schema does not have, so this endpoint — which resolves the production ApplicationVersion — never saw it.

Drop the required `pages` array. A manifest with no pages renders nothing, so persisting it bricks the app — and until now the server took it: the Design tab's refusal (REQ-OBPD-009) is a CLIENT guarantee and stopped at the browser, so an API caller got a 200. saveManifest now applies the same two structural rules AppRepoParser::validateManifest() has always applied on the GitHub-import path.
